title.narrative: Integrated WASH and NFIs Emergency Response to the Floods Affected Populations in Tokar, Red Sea State

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project aligns with the urgent needs of the NFIs, and WASH sectors, targeting 59,450 individuals (13,079 women,19,619 girls, 11,891men, and 14,861 boys) focusing on life-saving assistance for the flood-affected populations in Tokar, Red Sea State. The proposed interventions aim to increase access to clean water through the rehabilitation of 1nbspMWYs and f 4 hand-dug wells, water trucking, development of 3 borehole sources, operation and maintenance of 4 existing boreholes and the network pipeline, water quality monitoring and chlorination of 11 water points across Toker. Provide timely and appropriate non-food items for the most affected HHs in Toker, in addition to implementing sanitation infrastructure, distributing latrine items, and conducting rehabilitation, LM will organize sanitation cleanup campaigns, vector control initiatives, hygiene training sessions, awareness programs, and installnbspsignboards. These efforts will promote safe sanitation practices and prevent disease outbreaks. The involvement of the community will be prioritized to ensure sustainability and long-term impact, fostering ownership and responsibility for maintaining a healthy environment.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project aims to enhance access to basic water services, including drinking water, for flood-affected communities in Toker locality, reaching at least 42,500 people (9,775 men, 11,050 women, 10,200 boys, and 11,475 girls). It focuses on improving sanitation and hygiene to prevent waterborne diseases, involving the community in training Water Management Committees for sustainability. Additionally, the project will provide timely non-food item assistance to 3,390 households (16,950 individuals) through registration, distribution of NFI kits, and post-distribution monitoring, ensuring effective utilization and meeting the population's basic needs.lt/pgtltpgtThe project is designed based on NFIs, WASH cluster, and technical working group recommendations, and in close coordination with the HAC and line ministries in Red Sea State. Project activities will depend on findings from consultations between OCHA and the WASH, and NFI clusters, as discussed in the last meeting conducted by OCHA and SHF with implementing partners. Additionally, the design of this project directly aligns with SHF's priorities in targeting the most critical localities in need.ltbrgtThis project will be implemented with local partner ADD. Currently, LMI/IAS and ADDD are jointly implementing a WASH response project funded by SHF, aimed at increasing the resilience of crisis-affected Affected Populations in Tokar, Red Sea State. While the project provides critical emergency WASH services, there remains a need for additional interventions to address gaps in the targeted communities in Tokar. These needs were identified through state-level cluster coordination, feedback from technical line ministries such as WES, MoH, and MoSW, and consultations with targeted communities in Affected Populations in Tokar, Red Sea State during regular coordination meetings conducted by IAS/LMI and local partners.ltbrgtthe activities are designed based on the conflict sensitivity measures to avoid doing harm to the targeted communities and maximize the impact of the proposed interventions, the planned activities were proposed based on community consultation and technical line ministries and selected the best fit lifesaving interventions in the targeted communities.ltbrgtLM and its partner ADD are incorporating conflict sensitivity throughout the project cycle as during the design process ensured that all activities are designed to avoid doing harm while maximizing the positive impact of interventions. The project prioritizes community consultations, collaboration with technical line ministries, and alignment with cluster recommendations to select life-saving interventions that address the urgent needs of the affected populations in a conflict-sensitive manner.ltbrgtlt/pgt
